items.title: Rahul Gandhi presser ahead of march: offers CEC to resign and turn approver; says opposition will file SC petition today
items.summary: Speaking at a press conference before the 1:30 PM IST Chalo Dilli march, Rahul Gandhi offered CEC Gyanesh Kumar the chance to resign and turn approver — asking him to admit he erred but is 'not the mind behind the mistake.' He said the CJI declined a meeting but asked the opposition to file a petition, which INDIA bloc leaders will file at the Supreme Court today. Gandhi claimed 50% of Delhi Police privately back the protests and alleged police are being asked to free 'RSS goons' who beat protesters; said anti-'vote chori' resistance has brewed 12 years and is crystallising now. He urged citizens to join at 1:30 PM at Barakhamba Junction, Connaught Place.
items.source_name: The Daily Jagran (live blog, INDIA bloc march to SC)

items.title: DMRC shuts 6 metro stations 6 AM-4 PM for march; heavy security at Barakhamba/Mandi House
items.summary: DMRC closed entry/exit at six stations — Rajiv Chowk, Janpath, Mandi House, Patel Chowk, Central Secretariat, Barakhamba Road — from 6 AM to 4 PM Monday for the opposition march. Delhi Police barricaded multiple central-Delhi locations; RAF, CRPF and Delhi Police personnel deployed at Barakhamba Road and near Mandi House.
items.source_name: The Daily Jagran (live blog, citing DMRC/Delhi Traffic Police)

items.title: Two new legal fronts: Delhi HC plea against Jantar Mantar closure; SC plea against alleged hooligan attacks
items.summary: A plea challenging the closure of Jantar Mantar for peaceful protests was mentioned before the Delhi High Court; the bench headed by the Acting Chief Justice agreed to list it on Oct 13. Separately, a plea was mentioned before the Supreme Court seeking action against alleged hooligans attacking protesters and lawyers during the ongoing Delhi protests. CJI Surya Kant separately said the court's doors are open to all.
items.source_name: The Daily Jagran (live blog, INDIA bloc march to SC)

items.title: March to start from Barakhamba Road; Akhilesh Yadav confirmed joining, Mamata expected
items.summary: The opposition's march to the Supreme Court will start from Barakhamba Road. Expected participants: Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, Priyanka Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav (confirmed joining), Rajeev Rai, Mamata Banerjee, Manoj Jha, KC Venugopal. Congress MP Jebi Mathur framed it as citizens marching 'not as a political party' to protect democracy.
items.source_name: The Daily Jagran (live blog, INDIA bloc march to SC)
